refutes.claim: No changed line refers to `SuppressSourceGeneration`. The fix only hardens TypeCollector's member loop: it adds `continue` after the mixed-key diagnostic and skips duplicate keys instead of letting `Dictionary.Add` throw. title: Receipts/DuplicateKeySilentlyDroppedTests.cs: edge-case test passes on head (2 tests): no defect shown; refutes 2 lens claim(s): logic-edge-1, logic-edge-2

refutes.claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards silently discard a member whose key duplicates an earlier member's key. Repro: a `[MessagePackObject]` with `[Key(0)] int FirstMember` and `[Key(0)] int SecondMember`, or two members with the same string key. Base threw from `Dictionary.Add`, a loud generator or analyzer failure; `DynamicObjectResolver` also rejects duplicate keys at runtime. Head reports no diagnostic, and the generated formatter serializes only FirstMember, so SecondMember's data is lost on every round trip. This also changes behaviour when `SuppressSourceGeneration` is unset, which the acceptance criteria forbid.

The same silent drop applies in the second member loop (the hunks at new lines 1163 and 1179). A duplicate int or string key there is also discarded without a diagnostic, so the defect is not confined to the first loop.
